questions.question: In how many years will a sum of ₹ 5000 yield a simple interest of ₹ 2000 at an interest rate of 10 p.a.?
questions.questionHtml: In how many years will a sum of ₹ 5000 yield a simple interest of ₹ 2000 at an interest rate of 10 p.a.?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum = Rs. 5000

Simple interest = Rs. 2000

Rate of interest = 10%

Formula used:

\(SI = \frac{{P × {\rm{R}} × {\rm{T}}}}{{100}}\)

Calculations:

Let the sum be invested for T years

⇒ 2000 = (5000 × 10 × T)/100

⇒ 2000 = 500T

⇒ T = 20/5

⇒ T = 4 years

∴ The sum of Rs. 5000 earns a simple interest of Rs. 2000 in 4 years

questions.questionHtml: If the simple interest for 9 years be equal to 45% of the principal, then the rate of interest per annum is equal to:

Formula:

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time period

SI = PNR/100

Calculation:

5% amount increases in 1 year.

∴ Rate of interest is 5%.

questions.question: If the simple interest on ₹7,200 in 3 years at the rate of 16% per annum equals the simple interest on ₹9,600 at the rate of x% per annum in 4 years. The value of x is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If the simple interest on ₹7,200 in 3 years at the rate of 16% per annum equals the simple interest on ₹9,600 at the rate of x% per annum in 4 years. The value of x is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the simple interest is equal in both cases, the products of their Principal, Rate, and Time must be equal.

P1 × R1 × T1 = P2 × R2 × T2

7200 × 16 × 3 = 9600 × x × 4

345600 = 38400 × x ⇒ x = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal 1 (P1) = ₹7,200, Rate 1 (R1) = 16%, Time 1 (T1) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P2) = ₹9,600, Rate 2 (R2) = x%, Time 2 (T2) = 4 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ SI1 = (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

According to the question, SI1 = SI2

⇒ (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100 = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 72 × 48 = 96 × 4x

⇒ 3456 = 384x

⇒ x = 3456 ÷ 384

⇒ x = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated strictly on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period. The formula used is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Constant Interest Concept

When the simple interest obtained from two different investments is completely equal, their respective (P × R × T) products must balance out equally.

Amount

The amount refers to the total final sum of the principal and the simple interest earned over the given duration. Formula: A = P + SI = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

questions.question: In how much time will a sum of Rs. 12500 amounts to Rs. 20000 at the rate of 8 percent per annum at simple interest?
questions.questionHtml: In how much time will a sum of Rs. 12500 amounts to Rs. 20000 at the rate of 8 percent per annum at simple interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 12500

Final Amount (A) = Rs. 20000

Rate of interest (r) = 8% per annum

Concept:

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100. We rearrange this formula to solve for Time.

Calculation:

Simple Interest = Final Amount - Principal

⇒ Rs. 20000 - Rs. 12500 = Rs. 7500

Time = (Simple Interest × 100) / (Principal × Rate)

⇒ (7500 × 100) / (12500 × 8) = 7.5 years

Hence, it will take 7.5 years for the sum to amount to Rs. 20000.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2,000 becomes Rs. 3,120 in two years at a certain rate of simple interest. What is the rate of the interest per annum ?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 2,000 becomes Rs. 3,120 in two years at a certain rate of simple interest. What is the rate of the interest per annum ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Simple Interest for 2 years = 3,120 − 2,000 = ₹1,120

Interest for 1 year = 1,120 ÷ 2 = ₹560

Rate of Interest = (Interest per year ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (560 ÷ 2,000) × 100 = 28%

∴ The correct answer is 28% per annum.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2,000

Amount (A) = ₹3,120

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculations:

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 3,120 − 2,000 = ₹1,120

⇒ 1,120 = (2,000 × R × 2) / 100

⇒ 1,120 = 20 × R × 2

⇒ 1,120 = 40 × R

⇒ R = 1,120 / 40

⇒ R = 28%

∴ The correct answer is 28% per annum.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Concept

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial Principal amount. The interest remains constant every year if the rate and principal do not change.

Rate of Interest Calculation

The Rate of Interest (R) can be found using the formula R = (SI × 100) / (P × T), where SI is the total interest earned over time T.

Relation between Amount and Principal

The total Amount (A) at the end of the period is always the sum of the Principal (P) and the total Simple Interest (SI) earned.

questions.questionHtml: The sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹750 in 3 years and to ₹825 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.solution:
Simple interest for 1 year = 825 – 750 = 75

The sum is = 750 – 75 × 3

⇒ ₹525

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 14% p.a. is ₹4,200 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 5 years at the same rate. Find the sum.
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 14% p.a. is ₹4,200 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 5 years at the same rate. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
Let the principal amount be P. ​So according to the question,

(P × 14 × 5)/100 - (P × 14 × 3)/100 = 4200

⇒ (P × 14 × 2)/100 = 4200

⇒ P = 15000

questions.question: The ratio of the profits of P and Q is 5 : 8. What is their investment ratio, if their investment time period ratio 3 : 5 ?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the profits of P and Q is 5 : 8. What is their investment ratio, if their investment time period ratio 3 : 5 ?
questions.solution:
Let the investment of “P” and “Q” be “p” and “q” ⇒  \(p\over q\) × \(3\over 5\) =  \(5\over 8\)

Solving the equation, we get ⇒ \(p\over q\) =  \(5\times 5 \over 8\times 3\) or 25 : 24
